title: Assignment 1: Overfitting & Regularization
question: Explain overfitting, how to detect it, and two ways to reduce it, with an example.
referenceAnswer: Overfitting occurs when a machine learning model learns the training data too closely, including its noise and idiosyncrasies, leading to high training performance but poor generalization to unseen test data (high variance). It is detected by tracking training versus validation/test error: a widening divergence where training error continues to decrease while validation error increases indicates overfitting. Two common ways to reduce overfitting are: 1) Regularization (such as L1 Lasso or L2 Ridge penalty or Dropout in neural networks) which penalizes excessively large weights; 2) Cross-validation or Early Stopping (or gathering more training data/data augmentation) to halt training before the model over-memorizes. For example, fitting a high-degree polynomial (e.g. 15th-degree) to a small set of points generated by a simple sine curve with noise produces wildly oscillating curves between points that fit training points with zero error but predict test points terribly.
rubricRaw:
1. Definition of Overfitting (5 marks): Explains memorization of noise vs generalization gap.
2. Detection Methods (5 marks): Explains train vs validation loss curves and metrics divergence.
3. Two Reduction Techniques (5 marks): Explains two concrete methods (e.g. L1/L2 regularization, dropout, early stopping, more data).
4. Practical Example (5 marks): Provides a clear concrete example (e.g., polynomial curve fitting, image classifier memorizing background).

criteria.title: Concept of Overfitting
requiredElements: Defines overfitting as learning noise or memorizing training data
Distinguishes training performance from unseen/test generalization (high variance)

bandDescriptors.FULL: Precise, complete explanation distinguishing training fit from generalization error with high variance.
bandDescriptors.MOSTLY: Clear understanding of overfitting and poor test performance, with minor technical omissions.
bandDescriptors.PARTIAL: Basic notion that model works on train data but fails on new data, without addressing noise or variance.
bandDescriptors.MINIMAL: Vague or partially confused description of model error.

commonErrors: Failing to mention generalization to unseen data

criteria.title: Detection of Overfitting
requiredElements: Explains train loss vs validation/test loss comparison
Identifies the divergence point where validation error increases while training error drops

bandDescriptors.FULL: Clearly describes tracking learning curves (train vs validation loss) and identifies the divergence point.
bandDescriptors.MOSTLY: Mentions comparing train and test performance, but lacks detail on loss curve divergence.
bandDescriptors.PARTIAL: States that test accuracy is lower than train accuracy, without explaining validation curves.
bandDescriptors.MINIMAL: Brief mention of testing without actionable detection procedure.
bandDescriptors.NONE: No detection method explained or entirely incorrect.

commonErrors: Only mentioning checking training accuracy without validation set

criteria.title: Two Reduction Techniques
requiredElements: Identifies and explains first valid reduction technique (e.g., L1/L2 regularization, dropout, more data)
Identifies and explains second valid reduction technique (e.g., early stopping, pruning, cross-validation)

bandDescriptors.FULL: Names and clearly explains the mechanism of two distinct, valid reduction techniques.
bandDescriptors.MOSTLY: Explains two techniques, but mechanism of one is slightly incomplete.
bandDescriptors.PARTIAL: Explains only one valid technique properly, or mentions two without mechanism.
bandDescriptors.MINIMAL: Mentions one technique superficially without mechanism.
bandDescriptors.NONE: Fails to provide valid techniques to reduce overfitting.

commonErrors: Recommending increasing model parameters/layers to fix overfitting

criteria.title: Illustrative Practical Example
requiredElements: Provides a concrete scenario or dataset (e.g., polynomial regression, computer vision, housing prices)
Shows how overfitting manifests in that specific context

bandDescriptors.FULL: Provides a detailed, concrete example clearly demonstrating overfitting and its consequences.
bandDescriptors.MOSTLY: Good example provided, though the manifestation of overfitting could be more explicit.
bandDescriptors.PARTIAL: Abstract or generic example with minimal connection to overfitting dynamics.
bandDescriptors.NONE: No example provided or completely irrelevant.

commonErrors: Giving a textbook definition instead of a concrete scenario
